body.text:
ghaṭakarparakāvyam
śrīmanmahāmāheśvarācāryaśrīmadabhinavaguptapādaracitavivṛtyupetam
body.translated_text:
<s>Ghaṭakarparakāvyam</s> (The Poem of the Broken Pot)
Accompanied by the commentary (<s>vivṛti</s>) composed by the illustrious great <s>Māheśvara ācārya</s>, the venerable <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.

children.text: apūrvaḥ ko 'yaṃ te varada śirasaḥ śekharavidhir nanu jñātaṃ pluṣṭaṃ smaradhanur idaṃ mūrdhani dhṛtam /
children.translated_text: What is this unprecedented arrangement, O Boon-granter (<s>Varada</s>), as a crest-ornament upon your head? Surely it is known—this is the burned bow of <s>Smara</s> (the god of Love), held upon [your] crown!

children.text: yadālokāl loke viṣamaviśikhaḥ sphūrjatitarām iti prokte devyā galitaniyamaḥ śambur avatāt //
children.translated_text: For, upon beholding it, the one of uneven arrows (<s>Viṣamaviśikha</s>, i.e., <s>Kāma</s>) blazes forth all the more in the world— when the Goddess (<s>Devī</s>) spoke thus, may <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), whose restraint was dissolved, protect [us]!

body.text: idaṃ proṣitapramadayā hetubhūtayā proṣitapramadām uddiśya kathyate kulakam | tatra kiñcit kavinibaddhapramdāvaktṛkam, kiñcitkavinibaddhatatsakhībhāṣitam, kiñcit kavinibaddhadūtībhāṣitam, anyat kaviprakaṭitapratidūtīvacanam, itarat svatantrakavikathitam iti bahuprakāraṃ darśayiṣyāmaḥ | na tu saiva ekā kathanakartrī | proṣitaḥ pramado vallabho harṣaś ca yasyāḥ | athaca proṣitā vallabhena viyuktā, prakṛṣṭena yauvanaśṛṅgārajanitena madena ca yuktā | anyadeśatayā viyuktatvam eva proṣitatvena lakṣyate
body.translated_text: This is spoken by a woman whose beloved has departed (<s>proṣitapramadā</s>), who is the cause [of the poem], addressed to a <s>proṣitapramadā</s>—a cluster of verses (<s>kulaka</s>). Therein, some [verses] are the words of the separated woman composed by the poet; some are the words of her friend composed by the poet; some are the words of a female messenger composed by the poet; others are the words of a counter-messenger revealed by the poet; still others are spoken independently by the poet—thus we shall show many varieties. It is not that she alone is the single narrator. '<s>Proṣita</s>' [means] her delight (<s>pramada</s>) and her beloved and her joy (<s>harṣa</s>) have departed. Or: she is separated (<s>proṣitā</s>) from her beloved, yet joined with the intoxication (<s>mada</s>) generated by the excellence of youth and love. Being in another land is what is indicated by 'departed.'

children.text: chādite dinakarasya bhāvane khāj jale patati śokabhāvane /
children.translated_text: When the rays (<s>bhāvana</s>) of the sun (<s>dinakara</s>) are covered, when [rain] from the sky falls into the water—laden with grief (<s>śokabhāvana</s>),

children.text: manmathe ca hṛdi hantum udyate proṣitapramadayedam udyate || 1 ||
children.translated_text: and when the god of Love (<s>Manmatha</s>) rises up in the heart to strike— this [verse] is spoken by the <s>proṣitapramadā</s> (the woman whose beloved has departed). || 1 ||

body.text: dinaṃ karotīti dinakaras tasya bhāvane raśmipuñje chādite tiraskṛte sati tāsāṃ tamaḥpratipakṣatayā suprasiddhānām api sa sūryo yatra ācchādyate tatra kathaṃ harṣāloko 'pi mānaso 'stu, athaca virahiṇīnāṃ rajanisamayajanitaraṇaraṇakakaluṣitahṛdayāṇāṃ kadācit dinam api vividhavinodālokavitaraṇena bandhutāṃ yāyāt | adya tu yatprasādāt tādṛśadinam upajāyate tasya api kaścid ātmīyaḥ sahajaḥ svabhāvaḥ, so 'pi ācchadita iti sātiśayaṃ bhāgyahīnatvaṃ dyotitam | tathā jale ca ākāśāt patati | kīdṛśī | śokaṃ bhāvayati | jalaṃ hi nikaṭavartinā pārthivarajasā ātmānaṃ bhāvayati ekatayā yojayatīti śrutam idam, adya tu apūrvaṃ vartate śokena virahiṇīr bhāvayati śokamayya eva sampādyante tāḥ | na hi tāsāṃ prāvṛṭsamayamadhye priyāgamanaśaṅkāmātram api astīti tātkālaṃ nairāśyam eva khāt patatīty anena amuṣya duṣprasahasya apratīkāratayā sātiśayo 'nutāpaḥ sūcyate | tathā manmatho hṛdayapraharaṇaṃ prati sasaṃrambhaḥ | athaca bāhyo yaḥ kaścit hantā tasmād upāyaiḥ palāyyate 'pi, ayaṃ punar hṛdayāvasthita eva antarhananaṃ prati sasaṃrambhaḥ | caśabda ekakālatāsūcakaḥ | yathā kaścit durjano nirjane nirāloke durdina eva saśokaṃ janam ata eva nirudhyamānam ekākinaṃ prāpyaiva labdhacchidraḥ praharati, tathāiva amuṣmin kāla īdṛśam iva kāminījanaṃ madanas tāḍayatīty arthaḥ || GhkV_1 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'He who makes the day' is <s>Dinakara</s> (the sun); when his 'rays' (<s>bhāvana</s>)—the mass of his beams—are covered, i.e., obscured, [the meaning is:] for those [women] whose [hope is] well-established as the counter to darkness, even the sun is obscured there—how then could there be even mental illumination of joy? Moreover, for women in separation, whose hearts are agitated by the tinkling [of ornaments] born from the onset of night, daytime might sometimes become a friend through the distribution of the sight of various diversions. But today, even that sun, by whose grace such a day arises—even his own natural radiance is obscured; thus an excess of ill-fortune is indicated. And water falls from the sky. Of what kind? It produces grief (<s>śoka</s>). It is heard [in scripture] that water 'produces' itself—unites itself—with the earthly dust nearby; but today something unprecedented is happening: it produces the women-in-separation with grief—they are made entirely of grief. For there is not even a trace of hope for the beloved's arrival during the rainy season—thus the immediate despair is indicated by 'falls from the sky,' and the excess of anguish at the impossibility of counteracting this unbearable [situation] is suggested. And <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of Love) is intent upon striking the heart. Moreover, from an external assailant one might even flee by strategems, but this one, being established within the heart itself, is intent upon internal destruction. The word 'ca' (and) indicates simultaneity. Just as some villain, in a deserted, lightless, evil day, finding an opening, strikes a solitary, sorrowful, and therefore helpless person—even so, at such a time, <s>Madana</s> (Kāma) strikes women-folk who are, as it were, in such a condition. This is the meaning. || 1 ||

children.text: sarvakālam ativāhya toyadā āgatāḥ stha dayito gato yadā /
children.translated_text: Having passed through all [other] seasons, O rain-clouds, you have arrived when my beloved has departed;

children.text: nirdayena paradeśasevinā māriṣyatha hi tena māṃ vinā || 2 ||
children.translated_text: you will surely kill me, [left] without him, by that merciless one who resides in a foreign land. || 2 ||

body.text: iyaṃ nāyikāyā eva uktiḥ | he toyadāḥ ! macchokabhāvakajalavitaraṇodyatā yatra vayaṃ priyaviyuktā na abhūma, tādṛśaṃ kālam ativāhya yatra kvacit yāpayitvā yadā adya dayito gatas tadā yūyam āgatāḥ | tathā sarvaṃ kālaṃ diṣṭam athaca kṛtāntarūpaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathā matibāhyā amanojñamanasaḥpīḍakatvāt te ca toyadāś ceti vigrahaḥ | ataś ca māṃ māriṣyatha, kākvā uktiḥ | evaṃ nāma puṇyabhāginī bhūyāsaṃ, yena dayitajanavirahitā bhīṣaṇabhavadīyacaritāvalokanaparikhinnahṛdayā jīvitatyāgena api sukham āsīnā | athaca dayitena vinā yā jīvati sā avaśyavadhārhaiva | yaś ca dirdayaḥ san paradeśaṃ sevate, sa cet dayitāyā hṛdayaṃ praviṣṭaḥ, tatkaratalopanatam eva maraṇam | na hi asau jaladharasamaye kim api kāryaṃ kartum samartha iti avaśyam eka eva kvacana ciram āste iti | tasmād asmāsu upari prema tāvad āstām; dayām api yadi akariṣyat, tad avaśyam ihaiva āgamiṣyad ity etāvatī kaṣṭaparampareti anena viśvāsaparipāṭījanitadauḥsthityasūcakena dhvanyate || GhkV_2 ||
body.translated_text: This is the speech of the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) herself. O rain clouds! You who are eager to distribute water born of my grief — having spent the time when we were not separated from our beloved somewhere else, now that my darling has departed, you have arrived. Thus you are ill-fated in timing in every way, and unwelcome to the mind because of your tormenting nature — such is the compound analysis of 'rain clouds.' Therefore you will kill me — this is said with irony. May I be so fortunate that, bereft of my beloved and with heart pained by witnessing your terrifying conduct, I may find peace even through giving up life. Moreover, she who lives without her beloved certainly deserves to be killed. And he who is hard-hearted and goes to foreign lands — if he has entered the heart of his beloved, then death is merely the descent of his palm [upon her heart]. For he is not capable of doing anything during the rainy season, and so he certainly stays somewhere for a long time. Therefore, never mind love for us; had he shown even compassion, he would certainly have come here — such is the chain of suffering, and this [verse] suggests the distress born from the sequence of disappointed trust. (Commentary on verse 2)

body.text: priyatamaṃ prati nijāvasthāṃ jijñāpayiṣur bhīṣaṇajaladavijṛmbhām asahiṣṇur yuktyā kathaṃcid vacanāt yadi amī deśāntaraṃ vrajeyus tat sarvaṃ sampatsyate | priyatamo 'pi ca taddeśaprāptajaladharadhvānākarṇanena kadācit madīyām avasthāṃ svayaṃ vā anubhaved api ity abhiprāyeṇa nāyikā idam āha
body.translated_text: Wishing to inform her beloved of her condition, unable to bear the terrifying expansion of the rain clouds, [thinking that] if by some means through words these [clouds] would go to another land, then everything would work out — and perhaps her beloved too, upon hearing the sound of the rain clouds arriving in that land, might himself experience her condition — with this intention the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) says this:

children.text: brūta taṃ pathikapāṃsulaṃ ghanā yūyam eva pathiśīghralaṅgan /
children.translated_text: O dense clouds, tell that faithless one among travelers, you who swiftly traverse the path —

children.text: anyadeśaratir adya mucyatāṃ sāthavā tava vadhūḥ kim ucyatām || 3 ||
children.translated_text: Let his delight in other lands be abandoned today; or else, O friend, what shall be said about your wife? (Verse 3)

body.text: he ghanāḥ ! meghāḥ, athaca atinibiḍāḥ, ata eva hananaśīlāḥ, tam pathikānām madhye pāṃsulaṃ nirmaryādaṃ nirdayaṃ brūta | etad eva tasya abhijñānaṃ yat pathikeṣu madhye sa eva nirdaya ity arthaḥ | yato yūyam eva pathaḥ śīghraṃ laṅgayathety anena katham itaḥ kṣipram eva vrajeyur iti protsāhanā dhvanyate | brūteti ca adhyeṣaṇā iyam, laṅganaṃ ca ciravrajitasya api jhagiti āsādanam | priyatamo hi cirakālaṃ proṣitaḥ, sa katham yo mārgaṃ laṅghayitum na śakyas tena adya itaś calitena labhyeteti bhāvaḥ | kiṃ brūta | anyasmin deśe yā iyaṃ ratir vinā api kāryam āsaktiḥ, athaca vallabhāntareṇa saha premavisrambho na hi anyathā ambudharakālo 'tivāhya iti, sā ratir mucyatām | avaśyaṃ hi tayā ratyā bhavān grathita eveti upālambhagarbhā uktiḥ | adyeti | adyaivety arthaḥ | atha kathaṃ prema savisrambhaṃ śithilayituṃ śaktas tarhi sā tava vadhūr na punaḥ priyatamā, api tu śāstrasamayapatnī | kiṃ kathyatām, na vayam apriyam āvedayāmaḥ, niścitaṃ tu prāṇān naiva dhārayet | athavā sāthavā tava vadhūr ity etāvat sandeśavacanam abhidhāya kim ahaṃ kathaṃ vā bhaveyam iti kim alīkavikatthaneneti avaśyam eva na jīvāmīty arthaḥ || GhkV_3 ||
body.translated_text: O clouds (<s>ghanāḥ</s>)! That is, exceedingly dense, and therefore destructive by nature — tell that one who is shameless (<s>pāṃsula</s>) among travelers, that is, merciless and without propriety. This itself is his distinguishing mark: that among travelers, he alone is merciless — such is the meaning. Since 'you who swiftly traverse the path' — by this, the encouragement that they should quickly depart from here is suggested. 'Tell' is an entreaty, and 'traversing' means reaching quickly even what has been long traveled. For the beloved has been away for a long time; how could he be obtained today by one who has set out from here, when he cannot even traverse the road? — such is the implication. What should you tell him? 'This attachment — that is, clinging without purpose to another land, or else the love-intimacy with another woman — for there is no other way to pass the rainy season — let that attachment be abandoned.' For certainly you are bound by that attachment — this is a speech pregnant with reproach. 'Today' means 'this very day.' But if he is capable of loosening his loving intimacy, then she is your wife, not your beloved, but merely a wife by scriptural convention. What should be said? We do not convey unpleasant news; but certainly she will not sustain her life. Or alternatively: having spoken just the message 'O friend, your wife...' — what am I, and how shall I be? What use is this false boasting? — meaning: I shall certainly not survive. (Commentary on verse 3)

children.text: haṃsapaṅktir api nātha samprati prasthitā viyati mānasaṃ prati /
children.translated_text: The row of <s>haṃsas</s> (swans) too, O lord, has now set out through the sky toward <s>Mānasa</s> [lake],

children.text: cātakaś ca tṛṣito 'mbu yācate duḥkhitā pathika sā priyā ca te || 4 ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>cātaka</s> bird, thirsting, begs for water — O traveler, that beloved of yours is also suffering. (Verse 4)

body.text: yadi punar adya mārge gamanam āgamanaṃ ca na yujyate iti śaṅkyate, tad evaṃ brūteti nāyikā āha -- he pathika ! na hi bhavān nityaṃ yathā gacchati, ato yadā taddeśagato 'bhūt tadā sā priyā śrūyate sma | ataḥ cātakas tṛṣākrānto jalaṃ yācate, sā ca tava yāñcāṃ karoti | anena cātakayāñcāṃ prati jalasya kārakatā | tvaṃ tu tadīyayāñcāṃ prati na kārakaḥ | sa hi yāñcāṃ prati kārako bhavati yaḥ kadācit āśāpūraṇaṃ karoti | tvaṃ tu sarvakālam evaṃvidhapratikūlācaraṇacuñcur eva | tathāpi tu yācyase | ata eva āha na prabhuḥ paryanuyogārhaḥ | haṃsānāṃ sambandhinī paṅktir atibahavo 'pi haṃsā adya ākāśamārge mānasaṃ prati pracalitāḥ | eko 'pi hi yatra gacchati, tatra avaśyam aparasya api aniruddhena pathā bhāvyaṃ | kiṃ punar bahavaḥ | yataś ca jaladharamuktajalapaṭale te viyato bhuvi sañcaranti tasya yad ekāyatanam ākāśaṃ tad eva haṃsānāṃ mārgatvena vartate | bhūmau mārge ko bhayasambhavaḥ | yatra ca atidūraṃ mānasaṃ gantuṃ nirbuddhīnām api haṃsānām udyamaḥ, tatra parimitadeśanivṛttimātra eva na kim iti sā priyā bhavato yācate || GhkV_4 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] If, however, it be doubted that today, travel on the road is not feasible in either direction, then the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>) says thus: 'O traveler! You do not always travel as you do [now], and so when you were in that place, that beloved of yours was heard of [i.e., news was received]. Therefore the <s>cātaka</s> bird, seized by thirst, begs for water — and she too makes her petition to you. And thus, with respect to the <s>cātaka</s>'s petition, water has causal efficacy — but you have no causal efficacy with respect to her petition. For only he who sometimes fulfills a hope can be a cause with respect to a petition. But you are at all times ever the agent of such contrary conduct! And yet you are still implored! Hence [the verse] says: the master is not worthy of reproach.' The flock of geese — even a very large number of geese — has today set out upon the sky-path toward [Lake] <s>Mānasa</s>. For wherever even one goes, there another too must surely go on an unobstructed path — how much more so when there are many. And since they traverse the surface of water released by the clouds, [moving] from sky to earth, the very sky that is their single abode serves as the path for the geese. On an earthly road, what possibility is there of danger? And when even the witless geese exert themselves to travel the very great distance to <s>Mānasa</s>, then for the mere task of returning from a limited distance — why does that beloved not make her appeal to you? (GhkV_4)

children.text: nīlaśaṣpam abhibhāti komalaṃ vāri vindati ca cātako 'malam /
children.translated_text: The tender blue grass shines everywhere; the <s>cātaka</s> bird obtains pure water;

children.text: ambudaiḥ śikhigaṇo vinādyate kā ratiḥ priya mayā vinādya te || 5 ||
children.translated_text: the peacock flocks are made to cry by the clouds — what delight is there for you today, O beloved, without me? (Ghk_5)

body.text: nīlaṃ śaṣpākhyaṃ tṛṇaṃ sarvato bhāti, cātako nirmalaṃ jalaṃ vindati jalaṃ labhate, mayūrakulaṃ ca meghaiḥ kekāyuktaṃ kriyate ity etair vākyair pratyuta iha āgacchatas tava kim api pathi manoharatvam iti dhvanyate | nīlaṃ ca śaṣpam avalokayatas tatsukumāratarasparśānubhavasukhitacaraṇayugalasya gagananipatitāmalajaladalitaklamasya muditamayūraracitakekākaraṇanirbharavikasvarakarṇadvayasya avaśyaṃ sarvam eva sukham | adya tu tūṣṇīṃ sthitasya mayā vinā kā ratiḥ, na kācid iti svātmasaubhāgyasaṃbhāvanāgarbhā iyam uktiḥ | athaca mama īdṛśī avasthā yato vartate, tato māṃ prati śaṣpaṃ nīlaṃ malinasvabhāvam api komalaṃ karuṇārdram iva bhāti | cātakaś ca yo nāmnaiva priyagaganajalaḥ prasiddhaḥ, so 'pi jalam iha labhate, na tathā pibatīti pratīyamānā utprekṣā | ambudaiś ca virahihṛdayasphoṭanapaṭutaragarjitair api mamopari karuṇāvaśāt nijasuhṛtkulam ākrandavat sampādyate | kā punar mayā vinā mama abhāve kā aratiḥ kaḥ khedaḥ, na kaścit | tathā mama abhāve bhavataḥ kā iyaṃ ratiḥ ko 'yam anubandhaḥ, sā mriyatām iti | athaca prāṅ mayā vinā tava ratir na kadācid abhūt, adya tu kathaṃ sā ratiḥ | adyety anena prāg atyantapremarasamānasatām kapaṭena kila prakaṭitavān asīti dhvanyate | ata eva sotprāsaṃ priyeti āmantraṇam iti upālambhagarbhā bhaṇitiḥ || GhkV_5 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The blue grass (<s>śaṣpa</s>) called grass shines everywhere; the <s>cātaka</s> obtains pure water, i.e., finds water; and the peacock host is made melodious with its <s>kekā</s> calls by the clouds — by these statements, it is actually suggested that there is something captivating about your journey here on the path. The blue grass being beheld, the pair of feet delighted by the touch of its exceeding tenderness, the fatigue allayed by the pure water falling from the sky, the two ears fully blossoming with the <s>kekā</s> cries composed by the delighted peacocks — surely, everything is pleasant [on the road]. But now, for one who stands silent — without me, what delight is there? None at all — thus this is an utterance pregnant with the supposition of her own good fortune [i.e., her indispensability to him]. And further: because my condition is such, therefore to me the grass, though blue — i.e., dark in nature — appears tender, as if moist with compassion. And the <s>cātaka</s>, whose very name proclaims his love for sky-water, even he finds water here — [yet] 'he does not drink [it]' — this is the implied <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). And the clouds, whose thunder is quite capable of shattering the hearts of those in separation — even they, out of being overpowered by compassion toward me, produce wailing cries from their own family of friends. And further: without me — in my absence — what 'un-delight' (<s>arati</s>), i.e., what sorrow is there? — none at all! Likewise, in my absence, what is this 'delight' (<s>rati</s>) of yours, this attachment [to travel]? — let her die, then! And further: formerly, without me, delight for you never existed; but now, how [can there be] that delight? By 'today' (<s>adya</s>), it is suggested that formerly he had manifested, though deceitfully, a state of utmost tenderness of love. Hence 'O beloved' (<s>priya</s>) is a sarcastic address — and thus the utterance is pregnant with reproach. (GhkV_5)

children.text: meghaśabdamuditāḥ kalāpinaḥ proṣitāhṛdayaśokalāpinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The peacocks, delighted by the sound of clouds, the peacocks — grief-pipers with hearts of women whose beloveds have departed;

children.text: toyadāgamakṛśā ca sādya te durdhareṇa madanena sādyate || 6 ||
children.translated_text: and she, emaciated by the onset of the rains, is today being overwhelmed by unbearable <s>Madana</s> (Love). (Ghk_6)

body.text: amī ye bhavatā puraḥ paridṛśyante kalāpinas te meghānāṃ secanapradhānānāṃ sambandhinā śabdena muditāḥ kekāpriyatvāt, tathā ca proṣitānāṃ kāntānāṃ sambandhini hṛdaye śokaṃ lāpayanti samyak śleṣayanti avaśyaṃ, tathā proṣitānāṃ hṛdaye śokaṃ lapanti teṣu hi kūjatsu avaśyaṃ virahiṇyaḥ śokavatya iti niścīyate, tathā proṣitāhṛdayaṃ śokena lāpayanti dravīkurvate | sā ca te priyā adya ca tava durdhareṇa kāmena pūrvaṃ hi kāmabhayabhītāyās tvam eva śaraṇam abhūḥ, adya tu iha sthitasya tava madano durdhara iti durnivāraḥ | sambandhamātre ṣaṣṭhī, na tu kartari "khalartha" (2.3.69) iti pratiṣedhāt | tathā tavaiva sannihitasya sā toyadāgame kṛśā abhūt | āgamiṣyati jaladharasamayaḥ pravatsyati ca priyatamaḥ iti raṇaraṇakavatī bhavatsannidhāne kṛśā babhūva | adya tatra madhye bhūyān kālo gata iti asyā adya hitena bhavitavyam iti kavinibaddhadūtīvacanam idam | na hi meghānāṃ svayam eva "meghaśabdamuditāḥ" iti "toyadāgama-" iti ca svātantryeṇa kathayitum ucitam | "ambudaiḥ śikhigaṇo vinādyate" ity atre tu prāktanaśloke meghamukhasañcāritākṣarā nāyikā eva kavinā vaktṛtvena upanibaddhā, iha tu naivam || GhkV_6 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] These peacocks (<s>kalāpin</s>) that are seen before you are delighted by the sound associated with rain-clouds — whose chief function is watering — because of their love for their cries (<s>kekā</s>). And they cause grief to settle firmly in the hearts of those whose beloved husbands have gone abroad (<s>proṣita</s>); for when they cry, it is certain that women separated [from their lovers] become full of sorrow. Moreover, they melt with grief the hearts of those [women] whose [beloved] has gone abroad. And that beloved of yours — now, by [your] unbearable passion (<s>kāma</s>) — for formerly, when she was frightened by the fear of love, you alone were her refuge; but now, while you are stationed here, desire is unbearable...

children.text: kiṃ kṣamāpi tava nāsti kāntayā pāṇḍugaṇḍapatitālakāntayā /
children.translated_text: (verse 7ab) Have you not even compassion (<s>kṣamā</s>) for your beloved, whose locks fall upon her pallid cheeks —

children.text: śokasāgarajale ca pātitāṃ tvadguṇasmaraṇam eva pāti tām || 7 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 7cd) cast into the waters of the ocean of sorrow? Only the remembrance of your virtues sustains her.

body.text: sakhyā eva dūtītvena preṣitāyā iyaṃ bhaṇitiḥ | āstāṃ tāvat premānubandhaḥ | tādṛśī api yā kāntā lāvaṇyadyasādhāraṇabhūtā, sā yadi īdṛśavat jāyate, tat kiṃ tayā hetubhūtayā kṣamā api nāsti | pānḍuracchāyayoḥ kapolayoḥ patitā alakāntā yasyāḥ tadīyakapolatalapāṇḍimānaṃ malinasvabhāvā alakā api prekṣituṃ na pārayantīty arthaḥ | athaca kānteti āmantraṇam api | tvaṃ yadi tasyā vallabhas tayā īdṛśyā janamātrakṛpābhājanabhūtayā api yā sāmānyajanasya kṛpā bhavati, sāpi na asti tava ātmani iyatāpi puruṣaguṇaṃ bahumānaṃ vahato 'pi | tathāpi sā śokārṇavapānīye meghasamayavāriṇā pātitā bhavadīyaguṇasmaraṇena eva rakṣyate | athaca tvattas tava sakāśāt patitā śoke, bhavadviprayuktā ca jātā, śokajaladhau ca nimagnā sampannety arthaḥ | cakārād etad dhvanyate, vastutas tu tvadguṇānām eva sātiśayasambhogādīnāṃ smaraṇena eva śoke patitā | adya tu tathā kṛpāpātratāṃ prāptā, yad uta tena niṣkaruṇena pātitā api tvadguṇasmaraṇena eva rakṣyate | mama kila sa priyatamo 'pagato nirbahumāno māṃ prati ca dṛḍhatarapremapavitritāntaḥkaraṇo nūnaṃ mām eva tadavasthāṃ yathā pūrvaṃ trātavaṃs tathā trāsyate iti tvadguṇānāṃ smarantī sā jīvatīti yāvat | tathā yo 'yaṃ sāgare patitaḥ, so 'pi avaśyaṃ guṇasmaraṇavṛttyā eva rakṣyate dṛḍhaguṇaviracitarajjvavalambanena jātucid uttareyam apīty arthaḥ || GhkV_7 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is the speech of a female friend sent as a messenger. Let the bond of love be set aside for now — even such a beloved as she, who possesses extraordinary beauty (<s>lāvaṇya</s>), if she becomes like this, then do you not have even compassion, which [she] deserves as a cause [of pity]? [She] whose locks have fallen upon her two cheeks, pallid in complexion — the meaning is that even the hair, dark by nature, cannot bear to look upon the pallor of the surface of her cheeks. And '<s>kāntā</s>' can also be read as a vocative [addressing the lover]. If you are her beloved, then for her — who is such that even ordinary people's compassion, the compassion that arises [naturally in] common folk, is fitting — even that much compassion does not exist in your own self; [this shows] such [lack of] manly...

children.text: kusumitakuṭajeṣu kānaneṣu priyarahiteṣu samutsukānaneṣu /
children.translated_text: (verse 8ab) In the forests where the <s>kuṭaja</s> flowers bloom, deprived of [their] beloved, with yearning faces —

children.text: dravati ca kaluṣaṃ jalaṃ nadīnāṃ kim iti ca māṃ samavekṣase na dīnām || 8 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 8cd) and the turbid waters of the rivers flow — why then do you not look upon me, the wretched one?

body.text: iyaṃ vilāpāvasthāṃ yātāyāḥ svayam eva nāyikāyā uktiḥ | puṣpitāni kuṭajāni yeṣu vaneṣu yāḥ samutsukā utkaṇṭhitā mādṛśyas tāsāṃ yāni ānanāni priyatamaviyuktāni teṣu tadviṣaye nadīnām api kaluṣaṃ jalaṃ galati asmādṛśīnāṃ virahiṇīnām ānanāni avalokya jaḍabhāvānām api kaluṣaṃ jalaṃ galati, asmādṛśīnāṃ virahiṇīsaritāṃ śokāvilaṃ jalaṃ galatīty arthaḥ | tvaṃ māṃ dīnāṃ kim iti samavekṣase 'pi na | cakārāv apiśabdārthau bhinnakramau, eka nadīnām ity asya anantaram, aparas tu samavekṣaseśabdasya || GhkV_8 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is the utterance of the <s>nāyikā</s> (heroine) herself, who has reached the state of lamentation. In those forests where the <s>kuṭaja</s> (wild jasmine) trees have blossomed, the faces of women like me who are longing (<s>samutsukā</s>), separated from their beloveds—upon their [faces], even the turbid water of the rivers flows [as tears]. Seeing the faces of separated women like us, even the water of those insentient [rivers] flows turbidly; [or:] the grief-agitated water of [us] river-like women-in-separation flows—this is the meaning. Why do you not even look upon wretched me? The two uses of 'ca' have the meaning of 'api' (even), in different sequential positions: one [follows] 'of the rivers,' and the other [follows] 'you look upon.' || 8 ||

children.text: mārgeṣu meghasalilena vināśiteṣu kāmo dhanuḥ spṛśati tena vinā śiteṣu /
children.translated_text: On the roads destroyed by the rain-clouds' water, <s>Kāma</s> (the god of Love) touches his bow, [directing] sharp [arrows] at [the one left] without him;

children.text: gambhīramegharasitavyathitā kadāhaṃ jahyāṃ sakhi priyaviyogajaśokadāhaṃ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: O friend, when shall I, tormented by the deep rumbling of the clouds, abandon the burning grief born from separation from my beloved? || 9 ||

body.text: visṛṣṭāyām api dūtyāṃ tadvacanākarṇanād api na āgata iti śokākulamanasi nāyikāyāṃ yadā, kadācit sakhī tatsamāśvāsanāya ittham abhihitavatī -- mārgāṇāṃ duḥsañcaratvād asau na prāptaḥ, tadā punar api nāyikāyāḥ sakhiṃ prati iyam uktiḥ -- sakhi ! paśya , mārgā meghasalilena nāśitās tathāparo 'yaṃ doṣaḥ -- apratyayeṣu mārgeṣu śitā iṣavo yatra tādṛk dhanuḥ spṛśati, śitaṃ śiraṃ sandhāya ākarṇākṛṣṭaṃ moktum icchatīty arthaḥ | tena vinā tadviyuktāyāḥ | athaca yadi ahaṃ tam abhisareyam, tat mārgā durjñānāḥ, tathāvidheṣu api teṣu duḥsahaṃ smaraśarabhayaṃ smaraś ca tadvarjaṃ śarān sandhatte mām eva tāḍayati, anyathā kadācit tasyaiva gamanam iha sambhāvyate | atha ihasthā eva jaladasamayam ativāhayāmi, tat gambhīreṇa ghangarjitena jātatrāsā tiṣṭhāmi | ato he sakhi ! kadā ahaṃ priyaviyogajam śokadāhaṃ jahyām | ahaṃ ca meghaśabdavyathitā, madanaś ca niśitaśarapātanodyata iti avaśyaṃ mama jīvitāntena bhāvyaṃ | tac ca kadā bhavet, yatra ahaṃ sakalaśokanirmuktā sampadyeyeti | kecit sakhīpriyeti paṭhantaḥ sahṛdayāḥ katham adya api sakhī dūtītvena visṛṣṭā sā api na āgatā tat nūnaṃ tatsambhogarasalālasayā tayā bhāvyam iti sambhāvayantyāṃ nāyikāyāṃ kayācit vayasyayā mārgadaurātmye tadāgamanavighnakāriṇi upanyaste svayaṃ nāyikāyā idaṃ sūktam iti abhyūcuḥ | mārgas tāvat naṣṭāḥ tena ca vinā madanaḥ praharatīti tannikaṭāt calituṃ na yujyate 'syāḥ | athaca tatsambhogarasavṛttismaraṇenaiva madanakadarthanārhā ato 'haṃ sakhyā | priyeṇa ca saha viyogaḥ, tathā tasyāḥ sakhyāḥ | idānīṃ yaḥ priyas tena saha viyogaḥ, tajjaṃ śokadāhaṃ kadā jīvitāntena api jahyām || GhkV_9 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] When, even though a female messenger has been dispatched, [the beloved] has not come—not having heard her words—when the <s>nāyikā</s>'s mind is overwhelmed with grief, at some point her friend (<s>sakhī</s>), to console her, spoke thus: 'Because the roads are impassable, he has not arrived.' Then again the <s>nāyikā</s> speaks thus to her friend: 'O friend! Look—the roads are destroyed by the rain-clouds' water. And there is yet another defect: on the untrustworthy roads, [<s>Kāma</s>] touches the bow whose arrows are sharp—that is, having fitted sharp [arrows], he wishes to release [them], drawn to the ear. For [the one] separated from him. Moreover, if I were to go out to meet him, the roads are impassable; and even on such [roads], the unbearable fear of <s>Smara</s>'s (Love's) arrows [remains]—<s>Smara</s> fits his arrows at none other than me and strikes me; otherwise, his [the beloved's] coming here would sometimes be conceivable. Now, if I simply endure the rainy season here, I stand terrified by the deep thunder of the clouds. Therefore, O friend, when shall I abandon the burning grief born from separation from my beloved? I am tormented by the sound of the clouds, and <s>Madana</s> (Love) is intent upon shooting sharp arrows—therefore my life must surely end. And when might that happen, when I would become free from all grief?' Some sympathetic readers, reading 'sakhī-priya' (friend's beloved), [say that] when the <s>nāyikā</s> [thinks:] 'The friend who was sent as a messenger has also not returned; surely she must be indulging in the pleasures of his company'—when some companion [then] presents the difficulty of the roads as an obstacle to her return, the <s>nāyikā</s> herself [speaks] this well-formed verse. The roads are destroyed; and without him, <s>Madana</s> strikes—therefore it is not proper for her to move from his vicinity. Moreover, it is through the memory of the experience of his company that she deserves to be tormented by <s>Madana</s>—therefore I [suffer from the loss] of my friend. And [there is] separation from [that] friend along with [her] beloved. Now, the beloved with whom [there is] separation—when shall I abandon the burning grief born from that, even by the end of my life? || 9 ||

children.text: susugandhitayā vane 'jitānāṃ svanadambhodharavātavījitānām /
children.translated_text: By the sweet fragrance of [trees] unconquered in the forest, fanned by the wind of the resounding rain-clouds,

children.text: madanasya kṛte niketanānāṃ pratibhānty adya vanāni ketanānām || 10 ||
children.translated_text: [these] forests of <s>ketana</s> (Pandanus) trees, which are abodes of <s>Madana</s> (Love), appear radiant today. || 10 ||

body.text: yadā vinodārthaṃ sakhyā udyānopavanaṃ nītā, tadā taddarśanadviguṇataropacitavilāpāvasthāyā nāyikāyā idaṃ sūktam | ketananāmnāṃ tarūṇāṃ vanāni adya virājante | kīdṛśānām | suṣṭhu saurabheṇa vanamadhye kenacid ajitānāṃ, tathā garjatāṃ meghānāṃ pavanena vījitānāṃ prabodhitānām | ata eva kāmasya kṛte niketanānāṃ saṅketadhāmnām | ayam abhiprāyaḥ -- ketanavanāni madananiveśanasthānānīti atisukumārāṇi, jaladhararasitatadvimuktaśīkarāsārasahitaś ca pavanas teṣām eva prabodhanahetutayā sukumāratām āpta iti kim atra jaladasamaye mārgavaiṣamyam, tat nūnam eva ketanavānāvalokanaprabodhitamadanasthānasukhasaṃskāraḥ priyatama āgamiṣyatīti sambhāvayantyā nāyikāyā bhaṇitiḥ pratibhātīti | apare tu vanaśabdapaunaruktyam amṛṣyamāṇā madanasya avane rakṣaṇe kṛte ajitānāṃ ketanānāṃ vanāni śobhante iti āhuḥ | athavā saurabheṇa ye vane ekānte yatra aparaḥ paritrātā na sambhāvyate tatra jitā apahṛtadhairyavṛttayaḥ kṛtā vimohitāḥ kecana virahijanāḥ teṣāṃ daivavaśāt jaladharaśiśirapavanaprabodhitānām api punar api etāni ketanavanāni kāmasya kṛte karaṇāya pratibhānti | madanātaṅkakaraṇād ṛte na eteṣāṃ kim api prayojanam iti yāvat | svanaśabdena karuṇāvaśāt śabdāyamānatā dhvanyate | yadā svananto garjanto 'mbhodharā yatra saṃjātakṛpāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ, tatra amīṣāṃ ketanavanānāṃ kā iyaṃ niṣkaruṇatā || GhkV_10 ||

children.text: tat sādhu yat tvāṃ sutaruṃ sasarja prajāpatiḥ kāmanivāsa sarja /
tvaṃ mañjarībhiḥ pravaro vanānāṃ netrotsavaś cāsi sayauvanānām || 11 ||

body.text: iyam anantaravad eva uktiḥ | he sarjanāmadheya ! prajāpatir yat tvām sasarja śobhanaṃ taruṃ, tat sādhu, yatas tvaṃ kāmasya nivāsaḥ | kākur iyaṃ evaṃ dhvanati -- prajānāṃ kila patyā avaśyaṃ prajāhitakāriṇā bhavitavyam, evaṃvidhahṛdayadāhavitaraṇaniḥśeṣitanikhilajantoḥ kāmasya nivāsabhūtaṃ bhavantaṃ nirmimāṇena prajāpatinā suṣṭhu prajāpatitvam uddarśitaṃ, tvayi dṛṣṭamātra eva mama kāpi vyathā vijṛmbhate ity arthaḥ | atha evaṃ api jānatī kim iti mām avalokitavaty asīti yadi, tat kila mañjarībhir bhavān sakalavanamadhye śreṣṭho bahvībhiḥ kantābhis tu parivṛta iti śṛṅgāriṇi bhavati bahumāna ity arthaḥ, tathāpi sayauvanānāṃ yuvatīnāṃ tu netrotsavaḥ | yadā kila ahaṃ yuvatiḥ priyasaṃyuktā tvām avalokitavatī, tadā lokottaranayanānandavatī abhūvam, adya tvam evaṃvidhabahutaravallabhāparivṛto bhūtvā kathaṃ māṃ priyaviyuktāṃ trātavyāṃ darśanamātreṇa api madanaparavaśāṃ karoṣīti vākyārthaḥ || GhkV_11 ||

children.text: navakadamba śiro 'vanatāsmi te vasati vo madanaḥ kusumasmite /
kuṭaja kiṃ kusumair avahasyate praṇipatāmi ca duṣprahasya te || 12 ||

body.text: yadā sarjataror apakrāntā nāyikā jhagiti kadambam avalokayati, tadā prāktanamadanabhayabhītimatī jhagiti āha -- he navakadamba ! idānīm eva avalokitānubhūtatvadīyapratāpā ahaṃ tubhyaṃ śirasā avanatā asmi | evaṃ yāvat bhaṇati, tāvat tadīyakusumavilokanajanitaraṇaraṇakā āha -- yuṣmākaṃ puṣpavikāse kāmo vasati, mayā jñātaṃ sarjasyaiva idaṃ vaiṣamyaṃ yāvatā tvam api evam eva, sarveṣām ekayogakṣamateti sarvathā mama hātāśāyā nayanaviṣayatākṣamaṃ na kiñcit samastīti va iti bahuvacanena dhvanyate | itthamākārayatnī eva nāyikā yadā kusumitaṃ jhagiti kuṭajam avalokayati, tadā manyate nūnaṃ mām ayaṃ sarvato hi hatabhāgadheyām apahasatīti tata āha -- he kuṭaja ! kim iti avāṅmukhaṃ kṛtvā hasyate | kusumito 'pi pradeśo 'vaśyaṃ dharābhimukhaḥ, yaś ca sannihita eva param apahasati, so 'pi avāṅmukha eva | ataś ca tvayi upacīyamāne bahutaravyathā | te duḥsahasya praṇāma eva śobhana iti kākuḥ | ata eva īpsitatamatvābhāvaḥ sambandhaṣaṣṭhyā vyajyate | kiṃkusumair iti kutsitaiḥ parātaṅkavitaraṇacaturaiḥ puṣpair avahasyate iti sotprāsaṃ kākvā dhvanito 'rthaḥ || GhkV_12 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] When the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>), having departed from the <s>sarja</s> tree, suddenly beholds the <s>kadamba</s>, then, fearful from the previous dread of love, she suddenly says: 'O new <s>kadamba</s>! Having just now experienced your might, I bow my head to you.' Even as she speaks thus, [hearing] the tinkling sound produced by the sight of its blossoms, she says: 'In the blossoming of your flowers, <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love) dwells — I have understood it! This is the very same hostility of the <s>sarja</s> tree, since you too are just like it; all [trees] are equally capable [of tormenting me].' Thus the use of the plural suggests: 'In every way, for me who has lost all hope, nothing remains that is fit to be seen by my eyes.'

children.text: taruvara vinatāsmi te sadāhaṃ hṛdayaṃ me prakaroṣi kiṃ sadāham /
children.translated_text: (verse 13ab) O best of trees! I am always bowed before you — why then do you make my heart burn constantly?

children.text: tava puṣpanirīkṣitāpadehaṃ visṛjeyaṃ sahasaiva nīpa deham || 13 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 13cd) Seeing your flowers, I would suddenly abandon this body untimely, O <s>Nīpa</s> tree!

body.text: he nīpābhidhāna taruśrṣṭha ! tava sarvakālam ahaṃ praṇatā, tat kim adya mama hṛdayaṃ dāhayuktaṃ prakarṣeṇa karoṣi | anye 'pi taravo na evaṃ māṃ dahanti yathā tvaṃ sarvakālam abhiṣṭuto 'pi, sarvathā ayaṃ bhāgadheyaviparyayaḥ | athaca tava sadā ahaṃ praṇatā yena īdṛśaḥ upakāras tvat sambhāvyate, tvadīyapuṣpair nirīkṣitā dehaṃ visṛjeyam | kīdṛśam | apade 'kāṇḍa eva īhā dūtīvisarjanatatpratipālanamudhāvinodanaprabhṛtayo yasya tam | ahaṃ tāvat tādṛgupakāribhavadīyakusumāvalokane 'pi asamarthā, tāni tu yadi mahāpuruṣatayā evaṃvidhām avasthāṃ prāptāṃ mām avalokeyuḥ, tat ciravāñchitajīvitatyāgamanorathena api jhagiti yujyeya | atas tava sadā natā asmi | na ca evaṃ sambhāvanīyam -- ahito hṛdayadāhakāri kathaṃ praṇamyate iti yataḥ kiṃ tvaṃ hṛdayaṃ sadāhaṃ karoṣi, kākvā na evam ity arthaḥ | nijena eva virahahutavahena mama dahyate hṛdayaṃ, tad idānīṃ dāhakena api dagdhasya kiṃ dahyate iti sambandhaḥ | yadi tu ahaṃśabdapaunaruktyaṃ sahṛdayāḥ kṣamante tadā evaṃ vyākhyā -- āpade viṣamavipadvahanārtham eva kevalaṃ yo mama dehas taṃ tyajeyam iti | tathā nīpa taruvara tava natā asmi | evam uktvā duḥsahatayā dvitīyavākyam āha -- dāhayuktaṃ mama hṛdayaṃ prakaroṣi, punar api vilāpavaśāt, vicinitya brūte -- kiṃ yathā adya, tathā sarvakālaṃ tvatpuṣpekṣitā aham akāṇḍa eva dehaṃ tyajeyaṃ, kākvā naivety arthaḥ || GhkV_13 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] O [tree] named <s>Nīpa</s>, O best of trees! I am bowed before you at all times — then why do you today intensely make my heart burn? Other trees too do not torment me the way you do, even though you are praised at all times — in every way, this is a reversal of fortune. And also: I am always bowed before you because such a service is expected from you — [yet] having merely seen your flowers, I would abandon my body. Of what kind? — untimely (<s>apade</s>), i.e. suddenly, [abandoning] the efforts of sending messengers, awaiting [replies], and vain diversions. I am not even capable of looking at your blossoms, which are as [un]helpful [as that]...

children.text: kusumair upaśobhitāṃ sitair ghanamuktāmbulavaprahāsitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: (verse 14ab) Adorned with white blossoms that laugh like the drops of water released from the clouds,

children.text: madhunaḥ samavekṣya kālatāṃ bhramaraś cumbati yūthikālatām || 14 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 14cd) seeing the time of honey (<s>madhu</s>, spring), the bee kisses the jasmine creeper (<s>yūthikā</s>).

body.text:
ayaṃ bhramaraḥ bhramaṇaśīlaḥ yūthikaṃ cumbati, madīyapriyatamas tu pathika ekatra eva kvacit sthito mama nāma api na avekṣate iti | tāṃ kīdṛśīṃ yūthikāṃ | sitair baddhair na tāvat vikasitaiḥ, tato 'nantaraṃ tu ghanair muktās tyaktā ye 'mbulavās taiḥ karaṇabhūtaiḥ prahāsitaiḥ kusumair upalakṣitām | athaca ghanā muktāphalasadṛśā ye jalakaṇāḥ tatkṛtāni yāni prahāsitāni prahāsitatvotpāditāni nijacchāyāsphuraṇāni yaiḥ pītāni api santi śuklāni jātāni kusumāni | kiṃ kṛtvā madhuno makarandasya kālatām atyantaparipākarasotpannāṃ vilokya | athaca yo nāyakaś cirāt kāntām upabhuṅkte, so 'pi madhunaḥ pānagoṣṭhyāḥ kālatām avasaraprāptim avalokya paricumbati | kāla iti matvarthīyākārānto 'pi, tathā sā api kāntā dhammillapuṣpair ghanair muktāphalair virahasmaraṇānandādikotpannaiś ca ambulavair bāṣpair harṣacāṭvādijaiḥ prahasitaiḥ sitair baddhair vyāmiśrarūpatayā sthitaiḥ parasparasaṃśliṣṭair upalakṣitā bhavati kilakiñcitaceṣṭālaṅkārayoginī bhavati viśeṣataḥ pānagoṣṭhyavasare | yad uktaṃ
  "śuṣkaṃ muhuḥ praruditaṃ kṣaṇam aśrupātaḥ
  krodho muhur hasitam āśu ..."
ityādi | ata īdṛśī kadā ahaṃ priyeṇa paricumbyamānā bhuyāsam ity arthaḥ || GhkV_14 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This bee, given to wandering, kisses the <s>yūthikā</s> (jasmine), while my beloved traveler, stationed somewhere in one place alone, does not even regard my name. What kind of <s>yūthikā</s>? One marked by flowers that are white, tightly budded — not yet blossomed — and then, released by the dense [clouds], whose water-drops have caused them to burst into smiles. Alternatively, the water drops resembling pearls released by the dense [clouds] have produced a semblance of laughter, whereby even the yellow [flowers] have become white. How? By observing that the time for <s>madhu</s> (honey, i.e., nectar) has come — the time of utmost ripening of flavor. Alternatively, the hero who after long enjoys his beloved also embraces her upon seeing that the time for <s>madhu</s> (the drinking party) has arrived. The suffix '-kāla' can also end in '-ā.' Likewise, she too, the beloved, is marked by hair-flowers that are dense, by pearls, by tears born of the memory of separation and joy, and by smiles born of delight and coquetry — white and tightly intertwined, remaining in mixed form, mutually embracing — she becomes adorned with the <s>kilakiñcita</s> (mixed emotion) ornament, especially at the occasion of the drinking party. As it is said: 'Now dry, now repeatedly weeping, now a moment of tears, now anger, now laughter, now quickly...' and so forth. Thus the meaning is: when shall I be so embraced by my beloved? (Commentary on verse 14)

children.text: nicitaṃ kham upetya nīradaiḥ priyahīnahṛdayāvanīradaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The sky, having been reached and densely filled by rain clouds that scratch the heart-ground of those bereft of their beloved,

children.text: salilair vihataṃ rajaḥ kṣitau ravicandrāv api nopalakṣitau || 15 ||
children.translated_text: the dust on earth has been beaten down by waters, and neither sun nor moon can be discerned. (Verse 15)

body.text: idaṃ nāyikavisṛṣṭāyāḥ pratidūtyā vacanam | mā tvam adhṛtiṃ kārṣīḥ, mārgavaiṣamyād eva asāv iyantaṃ kālaṃ na āgataḥ | tathāhi nīradair meghair upetya sarvatodikkaṃ saṅghaṭya khaṃ gaganaṃ nicitam | kīdṛśaiḥ priyaiḥ priyābhiś ca ye vihīnā viyuktās teṣāṃ hṛdayāvanīṃ manobhūmīṃ radanti vilikhanti | evaṃ tāvat sarvatodikkaṃ duṣprekṣaṃ kṣitau bhūmau rajaḥ salilair vihatam | āstāṃ tāvad anyat salilena abhibhūyate rajomātram api na avaśiṣṭam ity arthaḥ || GhkV_15 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is the speech of the counter-messenger (<s>pratidūtī</s>) dispatched by the <s>nāyikā</s>. Do not lose heart — it is only because of the difficulty of the road that he has not come for so long. For the sky has been densely filled on all sides by rain clouds (<s>nīrada</s>). Of what kind? They scratch — that is, torment — the heart-ground, the terrain of the mind, of those who are bereft of their beloveds. Thus, the sky is impossible to see through in all directions. On the earth, the dust has been beaten down by waters. Never mind the rest — even a mere trace of dust has been overwhelmed by water and nothing remains — such is the meaning. (Commentary on verse 15)

children.text: haṃsā nadanmeghabhayād dravanti niśāmukhāny adya na candravanti /
children.translated_text: The <s>haṃsas</s> (swans) flee in fear of the thundering clouds; the faces of night today are without moonlight,

children.text: navāmbumattāḥ śikhino nadanti meghāgame kundasamānadanti || 16 ||
children.translated_text: peacocks intoxicated by fresh water cry out — at the arrival of the clouds, O you whose teeth are like <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers! (Verse 16)

body.text: he kundakusumasadṛśadaśane ! parivarjitatāmbūlādisambhoge ! pratidūtyāś caiva nāyikāṃ prati uktiḥ -- evaṃ nāma meghāḥ śabdāyante yat haṃsā api palāyante, rātrāv api na sañcaraṇaṃ yujyate yataś candrayuktāni tanmukhāni na bhavanti, ete ca śikhino mayūrā udgatapraharṣavaśāt śabdāyante | etena tat pratyuktaṃ yat tu nāyikayā pūrvam uktaṃ
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] O you whose teeth are like <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers! O you who have abandoned the enjoyment of betel and such pleasures! This is the speech of the counter-messenger (<s>pratidūtī</s>) to the <s>nāyikā</s>: the clouds roar so fiercely that even the <s>haṃsas</s> (swans) flee; at night too, travel is not possible since the faces of night lack moonlight. And these peacocks (<s>śikhin</s>) cry out with the delight that has arisen [in them].

body.text: "haṃsapaṅktir api nātha samprati"
body.translated_text: "The row of <s>haṃsas</s> (swans) too, O lord, has now set out..."

body.text: ityādinā mārgasaukumāryaṃ, tad eva hi pratyuta raṇaraṇakapradīpakaṃ mārgasaṅkaṭatāṃ karotīty arthaḥ || GhkV_16 ||
body.translated_text: — by this [earlier verse of the heroine about] the pleasantness of the road, that very thing on the contrary kindles agitation and creates the difficulty of the road — such is the meaning. (Commentary on verse 16)

children.text: meghāvṛttaṃ niśi na bhāti nabho vitāraṃ nidrābhyupaiti ca hariṃ śubhasevitāram /
children.translated_text: The sky covered by clouds does not shine at night, devoid of stars; and sleep approaches <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), who is served by the auspicious (<s>Śrī</s>),

children.text: sendrayudhaś ca jalado 'dya rasann ibhānāṃ saṃrambham āvahati bhūdharasannibhānām || 17 ||
children.translated_text: and the rain cloud with its rainbow (<s>indrayudha</s>), rumbling today, brings fury to elephants that resemble mountains. (Verse 17)

body.text: rātrisamaye 'pi gamanāgamane na yujyete, yato rātrisamaye vitāraṇ vigatatārāpaṭalaṃ nabho na bhāti yato meghāvṛttam | yac ca tayā uktaṃ "pathikapāmsulo 'sau mām upekṣate" iti, tad api na yuktaṃ; śubhasevitāram akaluṣacaritam api bhagavantaṃ hariṃ nidrā abhyupaiti aśaknuvatī virahaṃ soḍhum nāyakam abhisarati pratyutety arthaḥ | indrāyudhayuktajalado rasan śabdāyamāna ibhānāṃ kariṇāṃ parvatasadṛśānāṃ saṃrambhaṃ saṃrabdhatām āvahati samantāt darśayati | yaḥ kila atisukumāratayā suprasiddho jaladaḥ, so 'pi anyānullaṅghanīyena śakrāyudhena vajreṇa sātiśayabhīṣaṇaḥ sādinā hatānāṃ kariṇāṃ sādṛśyam udvahatīty arthaḥ | athavā meghaḥ śabdāyamāna ibhānāṃ kariṇāṃ parvatasadṛśānāṃ saṃrambhaṃ janayati pratigarjanaśaṅkayeti te 'pi kṣubhitāḥ sampannā iti sarvathā susaṅkaṭāḥ panthānaḥ || GhkV_17 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Even at night-time, going and coming are not proper, since at night-time the sky does not shine, being without stars, because it is covered by clouds. And as for what she said — 'that traveler in the dust disregards me' — that too is not fitting. [The commentary explains:] Even the blessed <s>Hari</s>, who is served by the auspicious and of unblemished conduct, [is approached by] sleep — [meaning] unable to endure the separation, the heroine goes forth toward her beloved, in the opposite direction. The rain-cloud endowed with a rainbow, roaring, displays on all sides the fury of elephants resembling mountains. That cloud, which is well-known for being exceedingly delicate —

children.text: sataḍijjaladārpitaṃ nageṣu nadadambhodharabhītapannageṣu /
children.translated_text: (verse 18ab) Upon the mountains where serpents are frightened by the thundering clouds,

children.text: paridhīraravaṃ jalaṃ darīṣu prapaty adbhutarūpasundarīṣu || 18 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 18cd) water falls with a deep rumbling sound into the caves — those [caves] which are beautiful with wondrously lovely [women dwelling within].

body.text: pratidūtyā eva iyam uktir nāyikā yadā evam āha nanu aham eva tatra yāsyāmīti, tadā tāṃ prati | darīṣu guhāsu api antaḥsthitā yā adbhutarūpasundaryās tāsu api upari jalaṃ patatīti vyadhikaraṇasaptamyau | kīdṛk jalam | saha vidyudbhir jalam dadati ye, tair meghair arpitaṃ, na te jalamātraṃ dadati, yāvat vidyuto 'pi atibhīṣaṇā arpayantīti | kva | nageṣu giriṣu garjanmeghatrastasarpeṣu | aparasya ye trāsadāyinas te 'pi yato jaladhararasitāt trasyanti, tatra kā vārtā bhavādṛśīnāṃ mālatīkusumasukumāramanasām iti tātparyārthaḥ | anyac ca kiṃbhūtaṃ jalaṃ | darīṣu antaḥ paritaḥ samantāt dhīro gambhīro ravo yasya, kandarāsu antaḥ pratiśabdena dviguṇībhūta ity arthaḥ | tena eṣā api āśā na asti -- toyadajalapaṭalaṃ gaganāt nipatat kvacana guhāmukhe 'tivāhya punar api gamiṣyāma iti || GhkV_18 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is the speech of the counter-messenger — when the heroine says 'I myself shall go there,' then [the counter-messenger speaks] to her. 'In the caves (<s>darī</s>)' — i.e. in the grottoes — even upon those 'wondrously beautiful women' who dwell within [them], water falls — the two locatives refer to different things [caves and women]. What kind of water? That which is sent by those clouds that give water together with lightning — they do not give mere water but also deliver exceedingly terrifying lightning. Where? Upon the mountains where serpents are frightened by the rumbling of clouds. If those who [normally] cause terror in others are themselves frightened by the thunder of rain-clouds, what chance is there for the likes of you, [delicate] as a <s>mālatī</s> blossom?

children.text: kṣipraṃ prasādayati samprati ko 'pi tāni kāntāmukhāni rativigrahakopitāni /
children.translated_text: (verse 19ab) Someone swiftly now appeases those faces of beloveds, angered by love-quarrels —

children.text: utkaṇṭhayanti pathikāṇ jaladāḥ svanantaḥ śoko vivardhati ca tadvinatāsv anantaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: (verse 19cd) the rumbling rain-clouds arouse longing in travelers, and sorrow grows endlessly in those [women] bowed down [by grief].

body.text: evam etābhir uktibhiḥ priyatamāgamanaṃ durghaṭam iti avagate āsthābandho nāyikāyā vijāghaṭītīty abhiprayeṇa sā eva punar āśvāsasampādanāya asya mādhyasthye viśeṣānuddeśāt tadīyahṛdayaśokaśikhiśamanaśaktām uktim abhidhatte -- ko 'pi anirvaṇanīyapuṇyasambhārabṛṃhitaḥ samprati jaladasamaye tāni kāntāmukhāni niratiśayasaundaryavanti rativigraheṇa praṇayakupitena sañjātaroṣāṇi tathā yāni tadīyaviyogajanitapāṇḍimnā adya āsādhāraṇadharmasundarāṇi kṣipram anāyāsena eva prasādayati tvām avaśyaṃ prasādayatīti yāvat | nanu na adyāpi asāv āgatas tat katham etat | āha śabdāyamānā hi jaladharāḥ pathikān raṇaraṇakavataḥ kurvanti niścitaṃ dinād dinam upacīyamānajaladharadhvānākarṇanena parivardhitotkaṇṭhaḥ priyatamas tāvad āgacchatīti yāvat | nanu priyatamāḥ kathaṃ śīghraṃ prasīdeyuḥ | āha tadvanitāsu pathikadayitāsu tathā śoko vivardhati vivṛddhavad ācarati yathā anantaḥ sampadyate | cakāreṇa evaṃ dhvanyate tad eva rasitaṃ tāsāṃ śokavivṛddhau kāraṇam iti || GhkV_19 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, when it is understood from these utterances that the beloved's arrival is difficult to achieve, with the intention that the heroine's attachment [to hope] should be broken, she — the [messenger] herself — in order to provide consolation, without particular reference to his indifference, utters a speech capable of quenching the fire of sorrow in his heart: 'Someone — nourished by an indescribable accumulation of merit — now, in the season of rain-clouds, swiftly and effortlessly appeases those faces of beloveds, surpassingly beautiful, that were made angry by love's quarrel — those [faces] which, by the pallor born of separation from him, are now beautiful with an extraordinary quality. [That someone] will certainly appease you —

body.text: atra kecid iti paṭhanti
body.translated_text: [Commentary note:] Here some read [a variant]:

children.text: tāsām ṛtuḥ saphala eva hi yā dineṣu sendrāyudhāmbudharagarjitadurdineṣu /
children.translated_text: (verse 20ab) For them indeed, the season is fruitful — they who, on days made dark with thundering clouds and rainbows —

children.text: ratyutsavaṃ priyatamaiḥ saha mānayanti meghāgamaṃ priyasakhi śvasamānayanti || 20 ||
children.translated_text: those who honor the festival of love together with their dearest — [happy are they]; but O dear friend, those [who do not] merely endure (<s>śvasamāna</s>) the coming of the clouds. (Ghk_20)

body.text:
ayaṃ śloko 'tratya iva na lakṣyate, pustakeṣu kena kāraṇena gata iti na vidmaḥ | tathāhi pūrvaślokaucityaṃ tāvad arthena na bhajate | tāsām eva saphala ṛtur varṣākhyo yāti yā sendrāyudhair ambudair durdineṣu priyatamaiḥ saha ratyutsavaṃ mānayanti | anyathā kila he priyasakhi ! meghāgamaṃ śvasamāḥ sārameyaprāyā api nayanti -- iti vyākhyāyāṃ prāktane nave (?) yamakam eva durlabham | dinadurdinaśabdābhyām arthapaunaruktyam api durdharam | yān astaṃ gacchann ino mārtaṇḍo yeṣu dineṣu -- ity api vyākhyāne tāsām iti apekṣito yadartho durupapādaḥ | tāsām iti tu anapekṣitayadarthe padavyaṅgye dhvanau vyākhyāyamāne uttaravākyaṃ khaṇḍaṃ gacchet caramārdhe cānyatheti (?) madhye śāstranyāyopacitaḥ kāvyāmṛtakāluṣaikakāraṇam adhyāhāraḥ kalpyaḥ śvasamā meghāgamaṃ nayantīti param anaucityam | na ca evaṃvidhena anaucityena kulakaparisamāptiḥ kriyamāṇā sahṛdayacetaḥsu romanthād ṛte kiñcit vidadhyāt | śvasatīti śvasas tadvad ācaratīti kvip tato 'pi tācchīlyādivivakṣāyāṃ cānaś | tataḥ priyasakhiśabdena sambandhaḥ prāg eva vā | tathāpi na kiñcid arthasya pauṣkalyam, kaṣṭakalpanāyasaṃ sat | kva | priyasakhiṣv iti saptamyā samāsa iti bahuvacanānte 'pi na kaścit kṛtaḥ sambandhaḥ | anyathāpāṭhakaraṇam api kleśamātraphalam eva | kiñca atra kartā mahākaviḥ kālidāsa iti anuśrutam asmābhiḥ | na ca asya kāvye tṛṇamātram api kalaṅkapātram utprekṣitavanto manorathe'; pi supte 'pi sahṛdayāḥ | tasmāt prāktana eva parisamāptiślokaḥ | sa ca sakhyā pratidūtībhūtayā nāyikāyā āsthābandhadārḍhyotpādanāya yujyate | utpannasamāśvāsā hi hṛdayaṃ sthāpayantī vipralambhayituṃ śakyā syāt
  "āsthābandhaḥ kusumasadṛśaṃ prāyaśo hy aṅganānāṃ /
  sadyaḥpāti praṇayi hṛdayaṃ viprayoge ruṇaddhi // (Meghadūta 10) //"
iti dṛṣṭyā | tena asya parisamāptidhurodvahasya api durandharatvam avikalam eveti | tad idaṃ yuktam ayuktaṃ veti svayam eva vidāṃ kuruta sahṛdayāḥ || GhkV_20 ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This verse does not appear to belong here; for what reason it has entered the manuscripts, we do not know. For it does not harmonize in meaning with the propriety of the preceding verse. The rainy season, named after the rains, is fruitful only for those [women] who, during dark days accompanied by rainbows and clouds, honor the festival of love together with their dearest ones. Otherwise — 'O dear friend, even the dog-like [people] merely endure the coming of the clouds' — [but] in this interpretation, the <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) in the prior and later [halves] is itself difficult to find. Moreover, the words 'day' and 'dark day' create a repetition of meaning that is hard to bear. [In another] interpretation [reading 'the sun that sets'] — the sense intended by 'of those [women]' is difficult to derive. But when 'of those [women]' is interpreted through word-suggestion (<s>padavyaṅgya</s>) in the <s>dhvani</s> [theory], without requiring the [explicit] intended sense, the subsequent clause would be broken, and in the second half, with '[they act] otherwise' [as a supplement] — a forced ellipsis, nourished by the logic of [the] treatise, the sole cause of contamination in the nectar of poetry — would have to be imagined: that 'they, dog-like, endure the arrival of the clouds.' This is the utmost impropriety. And a <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster) brought to conclusion with such an impropriety would produce in the hearts of the sensitive nothing but rumination [of displeasure]. [The word <s>śvasama</s>] — from the root <s>śvas</s> 'to breathe,' by analogy, with the <s>kvip</s> suffix, and then the <s>cānaś</s> suffix indicating habitual action. The connection with the word <s>priyasakhi</s> ('dear friend') would [need to] be [made] before [this]. Even so, there is no fullness of meaning — only labored construction. Where [<s>priyasakhīṣu</s>] is read as a locative plural, no connection has been made either. Making alternative readings is also merely a fruitless labor. Moreover, it has been heard by us that the author of this [poem] is the great poet <s>Kālidāsa</s>. And the sensitive readers have never imagined even the smallest blemish in his poetry — not even in their wildest dreams or even in their sleep! Therefore, the concluding verse [of the <s>kulaka</s>] is the previous one. And that [previous verse] is appropriate [as a conclusion], spoken by the friend who has become a counter-messenger, for the purpose of producing firmness of the bond of hope in the heroine (<s>nāyikā</s>). For one in whom renewed confidence has arisen, steadying her heart, can [then] be effectively beguiled — as per the insight: 'The bond of hope, like a flower, usually fragile in women, / stays the enamored heart that suddenly falls in separation.' (<s>Meghadūta</s> 10). Therefore, even this verse that bears the burden of concluding [the poem] — its capacity remains unimpaired. Whether this is fitting or not — judge for yourselves, O sensitive readers! (GhkV_20)

children.text: bhāvānuraktalalanāsurataiḥ śapeyam ālabhya cāmbu tṛṣitaḥ karakośapeyam /
children.translated_text: May I be cursed by [the pleasures of] lovemaking with women devoted in passion; may I, though thirsting, touch water [only] fit to be drunk from the hollow of my palm;

children.text: jīyeya yena kavinā yamakaiḥ pareṇa tasmai vaheyam udakaṃ ghaṭakarpareṇa || 21 ||
children.translated_text: may I be defeated by whichever other poet surpasses me in <s>yamaka</s>s (paronomasia) — to that [poet] I would carry water in a broken pot (<s>ghaṭakarpara</s>)! (Ghk_21)

body.text: kavinā auddhatyaprakaṭanāya sahṛdayajanamānasarañjanāya pratijñā iyam upanibadhyate | sañjātapipāsaḥ karakośena hastasampuṭena peyaṃ pānārhaṃ tāvad avasaraprāptam api jalam atyantābhilāṣautsukyapātram adrohayogyam api pratyuta ālabhya drugdhvā sahajapremapraṇayinīsambhogarasaiś ca śapeyam | atra śarīrasparśanākhyasya upālambhasya na atīva spaṣṭateti "śapa upalāmbhane" (Vā-911) iti ātmanepadābhāvaḥ | yena pareṇa kavinā yamakair jīyeya, tasmai ghaṭakarpareṇa jalaṃ vaheyam | karparaśabdena sātiśayakleśasamudvahatvam ātmani ucyate | atra ca yamakānāṃ vipralambhaśṛṅgārarasātiśayavighnabhūtānām api mayā tathā apṛthagyatnanirvartyatayā nibandhaḥ kṛtaḥ, yena pratyuta rasaparipoṣakaviśiṣṭavyākhyābhidhāyipadaparamparālābho yamakaiḥ sampannaḥ | tad uktaṃ
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] This oath is composed by the poet for the purpose of displaying audacity and for delighting the hearts of sensitive readers. 'Having been seized by thirst, may I [drink] water fit to be drunk from the hollow of the hand' — that is, water available at hand yet an object of intense longing, not deserving of hostility — on the contrary, having touched it, having milked it [without drinking], may I be cursed by the pleasures of lovemaking with women who are natural lovers [devoted] in passion! Here, the reproach called 'bodily contact' [i.e., touching the water without drinking] is not excessively explicit — hence the absence of the <s>ātmanepada</s> [middle voice], since the root <s>śap</s> [means] 'to reproach.' And 'by whichever other poet I might be defeated in <s>yamaka</s>s — to that [poet] I would carry water in a broken pot (<s>ghaṭakarpara</s>).' The word <s>karpara</s> ('broken pot' / 'skull') indicates the extreme toilsomeness [that the poet undertakes] upon himself. And here, the <s>yamaka</s>s, even though they might [elsewhere] be obstacles to the excess of the <s>vipralambha śṛṅgāra rasa</s> (erotic sentiment of separation), have been composed by me in such a way — as if accomplished by no separate effort — that on the contrary, the attainment of a series of words that serve as commentary expounding the specific enhancement of <s>rasa</s> has been accomplished through the <s>yamaka</s>s. As has been said:

body.text:
"rasākṣiptatayā yasya bandhaḥ śakyakriyo bhavet /
  apṛthagyatnanirvartyaḥ so 'laṅkāro dhvanau mataḥ // (Dhv- 2.16) //"
body.translated_text: 'That whose construction is such that [it can be] accomplished, being propelled by <s>rasa</s>, without separate effort — that is considered an <s>alaṅkāra</s> (ornament) in [the theory of] <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).' (<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.16)

body.text: iti | etayā ca pratijñayā etat parihṛtaṃ
body.translated_text: Thus. And by this declaration, that [objection] is refuted:

body.text:
"dhvanyātmabhūte śṛṅgāre yamakādinibandhanam /
  śaktāv api pramāditvaṃ vipralambhe viśeṣataḥ // (Dhv- 2.15) //"
body.translated_text: "In <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) which is of the nature of <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion), the employment of <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) and such [devices], even when one is capable, is a fault — especially in <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation)." (<s>Dhvanyāloka</s> 2.15)

body.text: iti | na hi iyaṃ rājājñā, api tu rasabandhavighnakāritvapramādaḥ parihāryaḥ | atra ca pratyuta ātmaparipoṣakatvam eva uktena prakāreṇa yamakānām iti | kavīnāṃ śaktir eva balīyasī, sā eva lokottarā vyutpattir iti abhidhīyate; na tu anyā kaviśakter vyutpattir nāma kācit | yad uktaṃ mayā eva raurave vicāre
body.translated_text: For this is not a royal command; rather, the fault of obstructing the binding of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) is what must be avoided. And here, on the contrary, the <s>yamakas</s> serve to nourish the self in the manner described. The power (<s>śakti</s>) of poets alone is supreme — that alone is called extraordinary learning (<s>lokottarā vyutpatti</s>); there is no other 'learning' apart from the poet's power. As I myself have said in the analysis of the <s>Raurava</s>:

children.text: "na vai doṣā doṣā na ca khalu guṇā eva ca guṇā
children.translated_text: "Faults are truly not faults, nor are merits indeed merits —

children.text: nibandhuḥ svātantryaṃ sapadi guṇadoṣān vibhajate /
children.translated_text: the autonomy of the composer instantly distinguishes merits and faults.

children.text: iyaṃ sā vaidagdhī prakṛtimadhurā tasya sukaver
children.translated_text: This is that natural sweetness of skill (<s>vaidagdhī</s>) belonging to that good poet (<s>sukavi</s>),

children.text: yad atrotpādād apy atisubhagabhāvaḥ pariṇataḥ //"
children.translated_text: whereby even from the production of [apparent faults] here, an exceedingly beautiful state has resulted."

body.text: iti śivam || GhkV_21 ||
body.translated_text: Thus. <s>Śivam</s> (auspiciousness). (Commentary on verse 21)

children.text: pramāṇapadamīmāṃsāgaganaṃ vai virājate /
children.translated_text: The sky of <s>Pramāṇa</s> (epistemology), <s>Pada</s> (grammar), and <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> truly shines;

children.text: samuccalati yatspṛṣṭaḥ sāhityāmṛtasāgaraḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: touched by which, the ocean of the nectar of <s>sāhitya</s> (literature) rises up. (Colophon verse 1)

children.text: kavīndor indurājasya te maccittavikāsakāḥ /
children.translated_text: May the rays of knowledge of <s>Kavīndra Indurāja</s>, the moon among poets, which cause my mind to blossom,

children.text: bodhāṃśavo vigāhantaṃ bhūrbhuvaḥsvastrayīm api // 2 //
children.translated_text: pervade even the three worlds of <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s>, along with the triple <s>Veda</s>. (Colophon verse 2)

children.text: tatparāmarśadhavalamanaḥkokanado manāk /
children.translated_text: He whose mind-lotus is made white by the contemplation of that [poet], <s>Abhinavagupta</s> by name,

children.text: kāvye 'bhinavaguptākhyo vivṛtiṃ samarīracat // 3 //
children.translated_text: composed a brief commentary (<s>vivṛti</s>) on [this] <s>kāvya</s>. (Colophon verse 3)

body.text: || iti śrīmadabhinavaguptapādaracitavivṛtyupetaṃ ghaṭakarparakāvyaṃ samāptam ||
body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Ghaṭakarparakāvya</s>, accompanied by the commentary composed by the glorious <s>Abhinavagupta</s>, is complete.
